_: Stored Discord gateway events, in the shape discord.js hands to a listener. These are the production call shapes described in commit 61f9f09: an embed posted by another bot or a webhook, message.content usually empty, the mint often only in a button URL. Replayed by scripts/verify-discord-replay.mjs through the real handlers, the real payload builder, the real route transformation and the real ingest RPC, so the chain is proven without waiting for a live call. No token, secret, user id or wallet appears here.

mints._distinct: The late embed and the accepted edit deliberately name tokens no other event in this fixture calls. Reusing one would be swallowed by the 60-second same-token cooldown, and the stage under test would silently never run.

events.name: buttonOnlyEmbed
events.why: The production shape. A companion bot posts an embed whose visible text is a symbol and a market cap; the address exists only in the Chart / Buy button URLs. A parser reading msg.content sees an empty string and the call is never journaled, with nothing anywhere recording that it happened.

embeds.title: BONK
embeds.description: New call from the alpha desk. MC $1.7M · LP $4.2M

events.name: webhookFieldEmbed
events.why: A webhook-authored embed with the mint under a CA field. The blanket author.bot filter that used to exist skipped exactly this, because a call channel is bots.

events.name: unapprovedChannel
events.why: The approval gate. A perfectly parseable call in a channel nobody approved must not reach the journal at all — not journaled and rejected, not seen.

events.name: ourOwnRelay
events.why: The relay embed this bot posts into its own log channel carries a mint. Skipping only ourselves — rather than every bot — is what keeps that from feeding back in as a call.

events.name: twoBareAddresses
events.why: A wallet flex next to a mint. With no link to say which is the token, refusing is the only safe answer — buying the wrong one of two addresses is unrecoverable.

events.name: replyInheritsParent
events.why: "aped this" under a posted mint is a call. The parent is a separate tier, so its addresses can never make the reply ambiguous, and the evidence label records that the mint came from the parent rather than the reply.

updates.name: lateEmbedOnBareUrl
updates.why: Discord attaches an unfurled embed to an unchanged message moments after it is posted; editedTimestamp stays null. A message whose only content is a bare URL has NO mint at create time and DOES have one once the embed lands, so treating this as noise loses the call entirely.

updates.name: realEditChangesMint
updates.why: A caller corrects the address. The original call is what a subscriber may already hold, so it must survive as a retracted record rather than be rewritten to a token nobody bought.

deletes.name: retractIngestedCall
deletes.why: A deleted call is retracted, not forgotten. Every call the message produced is marked deleted and none is destroyed.

deletes.name: ignoreNeverIngested
deletes.why: A blanket forward would open a raw signal and a rejected parse for every deleted message in the channel, burying the retractions that matter under ordinary moderation.

dexscreener._: One stored DexScreener token response for the primary mint. Three of its four pairs must be excluded: a non-Solana pair, a thin Solana pair, and a pair where the mint is the QUOTE side — that last one prices the other token, so taking it would record the call at a number nobody could have traded at.
